title: Dell PowerFlex Overview
description: This dashboard provides an overview of your Dell PowerFlex environment, covering system health, capacity, performance, and events across all components.

definition.content:
This dashboard provides visibility into your [Dell PowerFlex](https://www.dell.com/en-us/shop/powerflex/sf/powerflex) environment, covering system health, capacity, performance, and events across all components.

Use the template variables above to drill down from **system → protection domain → storage pool → volume → SDC/SDS -> device **.

Tracks overall system health including total capacity utilization, aggregate read/write IOPS and throughput, latency trends, and device errors. Use this section to quickly assess whether the PowerFlex environment is performing within normal bounds.

Tracks capacity, IOPS, and throughput per protection domain, along with rebuild and rebalance activity. Spikes in rebuild throughput or growing failed capacity may indicate disk failures requiring attention.

Tracks per-pool capacity, performance, and provisioning breakdown. Use this section to identify pools approaching capacity limits, spot latency outliers, and monitor rebuild or rebalance activity at the pool level.
Tracks per-volume IOPS, latency, throughput, and mapped SDC counts. Use this section to identify hot volumes or volumes experiencing elevated latency.
SDCs consume storage by mapping volumes from the cluster. This section tracks per-client IOPS, throughput, latency, and mapped volume counts to help identify noisy or slow consumers.
SDSs contribute local storage to the cluster. This section tracks per-server throughput, IOPS, latency, capacity utilization, and RF cache hit/miss rates to assess storage node health.
Displays PowerFlex events and alerts collected from the Gateway API on a timeline, alongside log volume by status. Log collection must be enabled for the logs panel to populate.
Tracks per-device latency, throughput, IOPS, capacity, I/O sizes, and error counts. Device statistics collection is disabled by default — enable it with the `resource_filters` configuration option.
